subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Out of the blue

options.text: Always dressing up in blue clothes
Coming out of a blue box

solution:
The solution is **Completely unexpected.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom "Out of the blue" is Completely unexpected.
 
• Let's see information about other options:
 
 
• Always dressing up in blue clothes - Indicates freshness, peace, and loyalty.
 
 
• *For example: "The women always dress up in blue clothes."*​
 
 
 
• Caught in a fight - A situation between two or more sides in an argument issue, often leaving one without a clear course of action to satisfy either side. 
 
 
• ​*For example: "They caught in a fight."*
 
 
 
• Coming out of a blue box - To happen unexpectedly.
 
 
• ​*For example: "He came out of a blue box on my birthday."*
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore **option 1 **is the correct option.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's discuss *idioms:*
 
• ​A group of words established by usage as having a meaning not deducible from those of the individual words.​*​*
 
• For example:- 
 
 
• **On cloud nine **- Being very happy.
 
• **Get your act together **- Get organized and do things effectively.
 
• **Back against the wall **- Stuck in a difficult circumstance with no escape.
